unwrapped.productDescription: A round puck of soap with NO wrapper and NO label of any kind — this is the bare bar as it is once unwrapped. Roughly two and a half inches across and about a third as thick, with flat top and bottom faces that are very slightly uneven rather than machine-flat. The colour is a warm pale cream or ivory, NOT white: an off-white body deepening to a faint butter-yellow band toward one edge. The material is semi-translucent and waxy, so light sits a little way into the surface instead of stopping flat on it, giving a low sheen that is neither glossy nor matte. The face is subtly mottled with faint cloudy streaking and a few small pale flecks, never uniform. The rim is visibly hand-cut: slightly irregular in profile, a little rough or crumbly in places, with small chips along the edge. There is NO printing, NO stamp, NO embossing or debossing, NO logo and NO lettering anywhere on it — the bare soap carries no markings at all.
unwrapped._note:
The bare bar, for in-use scenes only. A wrapped bar being lathered or sitting wet in a shower is physically incoherent — that is the package, not the soap.

PRODUCT-LEVEL, NOT PER-VARIANT (Sean, 2026-08-20): the raw bar is the same for every scent — the variants differ in what is added to the batch and on the printed wrapper, not in how the bare puck looks. So one reference set under imageDir serves calming-lavender, nourishing-tea-tree, refreshing-lemongrass and pure-unscented alike, and index.js reads it without appending a variant. The directory was first named pure-unscented-unwrapped, which wrongly implied otherwise.

ONLY A BAR HAS THIS. coconut-soap is the only bar in the catalogue; every other RSC product is a bottle or a pump, so there is no wrapper to be off and no unwrapped form to describe.

title: Coconut Bar Soap — 12-Pack
_unitCountNote:
SIX, and the product is TWELVE bars — a deliberate operator decision (Sean, 2026-08-26), not an oversight. unitCount drives the RENDER and the VERIFY gate only; it never reaches the copy prompt, so the type an operator sets still reads "12-Pack" and "$88" from the catalog entry, and the claim gate still sources both. The picture is a representative arrangement — the same thing the Health y Sol reference ad does, pyramiding six boxes while selling ten.

WHY NOT 12, measured rather than assumed. Two paid runs at unitCount 12 (2026-08-26, ~$2.34): us-vs-them passed on attempt 1 with a clean 3x4 grid, and the other two formats failed 6 of 6 attempts between them, ALWAYS on inventoryVerdict's unit count. The cause is the plateBriefs, which all say "the product stands upright" — written for a single bottle. At a high unitCount that has no coherent reading, so the model improvises, and the brief's PLACEMENT decides whether the result can be counted: offer-focused anchors to the "lower right at hero scale" and got an overlapping pile (11 of 12, twice, one bar cropped at the frame edge); problem-aware asks for "about a quarter" of the frame and got a stack the verifier read as ONE unit (4 of 12). Symmetric, centred, full-width briefs survive a high count; corner-anchored ones do not.

So this number is a workaround for a plateBrief limitation, NOT evidence that 6 is the right depiction. The root fix is a multi-unit arrangement clause in the briefs, which would also help foam-soap-bundle (3), coconut-oil-lip-balm (4) and both starter sets. Raise this back to 12 when that lands — and re-measure rather than assuming, because 12 verifiably DOES work on a grid brief.
_imageDirNote: Shares coconut-soap's reference photographs deliberately — the 12-pack is twelve of that exact bar, not a different product, and there is no photograph of twelve of them together. The variant subdirectories (pure-unscented/ etc.) resolve the same way they do for the single bar.
